ai.description: Pterorana khare reaches 6–8 cm. It is olive-brown with a pale mid-dorsal stripe and distinctive lateral skin folds. It is identified by prominent, wing-like skin flaps along its flanks.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Pterorana khare* is best distinguished by the distinctive, prominent longitudinal skin folds (lateral ridges) that run along the sides of its body, which are absent in similar species.
ai.habitat: Pterorana khare inhabits fast-flowing, rocky streams within subtropical evergreen forests in the Himalayan foothills, typically at altitudes between 500 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: Khare's Frog is primarily nocturnal and exhibits a unique defensive strategy by emitting a high-pitched, piercing scream when threatened by predators.
ai.reproductionNotes: Pterorana khare breeds in rocky streams during the monsoon (June–August), laying large, pigmented eggs in clusters attached to submerged stones.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Pterorana khare* is endemic to the high-altitude evergreen forests of the Eastern Himalayas, specifically recorded in the Indian states of Arunachal Pradesh and Nagaland.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Pterorana khare* consists of a series of short, high-pitched, metallic "tink" sounds, typically emitted from rocky stream habitats.
